liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Shakedown Street** (6 reviews): Reviewer calls this the best Shakedown Street they have heard, with a jam full of tension and release; Reviewer says the show is all about the Shakedown [30][32][35][36][38][41]
- **Keep on Growing** (1 review): Reviewer felt Keep on Growing drained the energy from the first set [40]
- **Gimmie Some Lovin** (1 review): Reviewer notes it was played mid-second set, followed by He's Gone into Cryptical Envelopment [36]

## Setlist highlights

- **Keep on Growing**: rare: 4 archived performances [42]

## The recordings

- **gd85-06-30.oade-schoeps.sacks.25242.sbeok.flacf** (recommended): source not stated; 22 songs; 155 min; rated 4.58/5 by 26 [1]
- **gd85-06-30.sbd.georges.366.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 147 min; rated 4.22/5 by 27 [2]. Said about its sound: Soundboard sounds a bit thin, like other summer 1985 soundboards in circulation, but still worth getting [32]
- **gd1985-06-30.akgC422.holbrook.burke.84246.flac24**: source not stated; 22 songs; 147 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [3]
- **gd1985-06-30.176640.senn.md41.strizak.flac2448**: source not stated; 22 songs; 145 min [6]. Said about its sound: About thirty seconds of Brown Eyed Women is missing with a rough splice; otherwise pleasant, good-quality audio [6]
- **gd1985-06-30.152702.akgc422.davis-murtha.holbrook.flac2448**: source not stated; 23 songs; 149 min [7]. Said about its sound: The whole show suffers from the 1985 PA distortion, later partly traced to Phil's pickups in his new six-string bass [7]
- **gd85-06-30.aud.oade-sacks.set2.7833.sbefail.shnf**: audience recording; 12 songs; 105 min; rated 4.16/5 by 19 [27]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the audience recording captures the distinctive Merriweather sound very well; Reviewer says audience recordings don't come better than this one [40][41]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended; the crowd stayed wild through the whole second set, until the anniversary banner was lowered at the end [35]
- Cab driver says he drove tour manager Robert Taylor from the Columbia Inn to Merriweather, stopping at Giant Food for salad bar fruit [37]
- Taylor asked the driver to find two Sony 2002 shortwave receivers; the driver was tipped and given backstage passes [37]
- Reviewer says it was still light out when Drums and Space finished, and dark when The Other One came out blazing [39]
- Stage EQ problems after Samson led the tapers to pause the tape; volume changed in the first three minutes [7]
- Reviewer argues that 1985 is unfairly dismissed by 70s-minded fans and that this show disproves it, with a strong second set [36]
- Reviewer considers this probably the best show of 1985, with a hot opening Half-Step into CC Rider [39]
- Reviewer thought the second night had better playing, though this show had the better song selection [40]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd85-06-30.oade-schoeps.sacks.25242.sbeok.flacf**: taped by Oade Brothers; transferred by Doug Oade - Darren Sacks; source: Schoeps cmc441 (90deg, 17cm) > Oade M118 > Oade mod SONY PCM-F1 [1]. Also: Master PCM went to a DAW via SEKD Prodif, then WAV, then FLAC via Darrin Sacks [1]
- **gd85-06-30.sbd.georges.366.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBDmc> DAT> CD [2]
- **gd1985-06-30.akgC422.holbrook.burke.84246.flac24**: taped by Kyle Holbrook; transferred by Tim Burke; source: AKG C422 (Cardioid) > AKG S42 > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell MX90 (No Dolby) [3]. Also: Tape flips occur during Looks Like Rain, 2:44 into Drums, and between the s2t12 and s2t13 tracks [3]
- **gd1985-06-30.176640.senn.md41.strizak.flac2448**: taped by Tom Strizak; transferred by Tom Strizak; source: Master recording by Tom Strizak (*first show with new mics) 2- Sennheiser MD441 mounted in standard stereo configuration Sony TC-D5M (dolby - On B) > TDK MA90… [6]. Also: Taper paused the tape between songs, losing some show context; the tape flip in Looks Like Rain is crossfaded [6]
- **gd1985-06-30.152702.akgc422.davis-murtha.holbrook.flac2448**: taped by Executive Crew;Mike Davis;Kenny Davis;Sean Murtha;Kyle Holbrook;Tom Pinney;John Borg;Gary Steel; transferred by Kyle Holbrook; source: Microphones: AKG C422 (Cardioid) > AKG S42 XY 90º Recorder: Sony TC-D5M Location: Lawn ~275' from stage (crest of the hill) [7]. Also: Fresh master takeoff made with a newly serviced cassette deck, replacing an older takeoff with flutter and channel swapping [7]
- **gd85-06-30.aud.oade-sacks.set2.7833.sbefail.shnf**: source: Daud -- Oade recording: Schoeps CMC441 (@ 90 degrees) > Oade M118 > Oade Modified PCM-F1 > DATs > CDRs > EAC > SHN (Seekable) [27]

claims.text: Reviewer calls this the best Shakedown Street they have heard, with a jam full of tension and release
Soundboard sounds a bit thin, like other summer 1985 soundboards in circulation, but still worth getting
Reviewer says the show is all about the Shakedown
Reviewer attended; the crowd stayed wild through the whole second set, until the anniversary banner was lowered at the end
Reviewer says the Shakedown rocked
Reviewer argues that 1985 is unfairly dismissed by 70s-minded fans and that this show disproves it, with a strong second set
Reviewer calls it the best version ever played
Reviewer notes it was played mid-second set, followed by He's Gone into Cryptical Envelopment
Cab driver says he drove tour manager Robert Taylor from the Columbia Inn to Merriweather, stopping at Giant Food for salad bar fruit
Taylor asked the driver to find two Sony 2002 shortwave receivers; the driver was tipped and given backstage passes
Reviewer calls it the best Shakedown ever, with a seamless transition out of the jam, setting up the later Cryptical
Reviewer says it was still light out when Drums and Space finished, and dark when The Other One came out blazing
Reviewer considers this probably the best show of 1985, with a hot opening Half-Step into CC Rider
Reviewer says the audience recording captures the distinctive Merriweather sound very well
Reviewer felt Keep on Growing drained the energy from the first set
Reviewer thought the second night had better playing, though this show had the better song selection
Reviewer says audience recordings don't come better than this one
Reviewer singles out the Shakedown Street
Recorded with Schoeps cmc441 mics at 90 degrees, 17cm, into Oade M118 modified Sony PCM-F1
Master PCM went to a DAW via SEKD Prodif, then WAV, then FLAC via Darrin Sacks
Tape flips occur during Looks Like Rain, 2:44 into Drums, and between the s2t12 and s2t13 tracks
About thirty seconds of Brown Eyed Women is missing with a rough splice; otherwise pleasant, good-quality audio
Taper paused the tape between songs, losing some show context; the tape flip in Looks Like Rain is crossfaded
The whole show suffers from the 1985 PA distortion, later partly traced to Phil's pickups in his new six-string bass
Stage EQ problems after Samson led the tapers to pause the tape; volume changed in the first three minutes
Fresh master takeoff made with a newly serviced cassette deck, replacing an older takeoff with flutter and channel swapping
